The sentiment is neutral as macroeconomic data is stable and markets seem to be waiting for new developments.

audio_script_it:
Buongiorno, benvenuti al Morning Briefing di Price Alert.

I mercati asiatici hanno chiuso la settimana con il Nikkei in rialzo del 2.81% e Shanghai in aumento dell'1.12%.

MERCATI OCCIDENTALI: nella seduta precedente, S&P 500 in rialzo dello 0.5%, VIX in calo del 9.05%, indice del dollaro DXY in calo dell'0.11%. L'oro ha guadagnato il 3.63%, raggiungendo quota $4238.8 l'oncia, mentre il petrolio è sceso del 3.37% a $87.33 Il rendimento del decennale USA è salito dello 0.54% al 4.48%.

Sul fronte geopolitico, si segnalano le sfide fiscali e finanziarie dell'Ucraina e le mosse della Russia, Cina e Iran per contrastare la pressione occidentale. Inoltre, il Giappone punta sulla scoperta di farmaci in Cina per crescita economica.

MACRO E BANCHE CENTRALI: nessun dato macro rilevante in uscita oggi.

Passiamo ora al comparto degli asset digitali. Bitcoin si mantiene sopra i sessantaquattromila dollari, con un incremento dell'uno virgola zero due percento. I flussi netti giornalieri negli ETF Bitcoin sono stati di circa ottantacinque milioni di dollari. Questo movimento potrebbe essere influenzato dalle recenti dichiarazioni sul possibile accordo di pace tra Iran e Pakistan.

Per quanto riguarda le altre criptovalute, Ethereum quota mille seicentosettantacinque dollari, con una variazione positiva dello zero virgola uno percento. Solana guadagna l'uno virgola due nove percento, arrivando a sessantotto virgola due dollari. BNB registra un incremento dell'uno virgola zero sette percento, a seicentodieci virgola quattro dollari.

Il Fear & Greed Index è a diciotto, in zona di Extreme Fear, suggerisce cautela sugli investitori.

Nessun dato macro in agenda oggi. Per approfondire i temi di oggi, sulla nostra piattaforma trovate gli articoli completi nella sezione Storie in Primo Piano. Grazie per l'attenzione e a domani.
audio_script_en:
Good morning, welcome to the Price Alert Morning Briefing. 

The Asian markets closed the week with Nikkei up 2.81% and Shanghai up 1.12%.

WESTERN MARKETS: in the previous session, S&P 500 up 0.5%, VIX down 9.05%, dollar index DXY down 0.11%. Gold gained 3.63%, reaching $4238.8 per ounce, while oil fell 3.37% to $87.33 The 10-year US yield rose 0.54% to 4.48%.

On the geopolitical front, Ukraine's fiscal and financial challenges and Russia, China, and Iran's moves to counter Western pressure are noteworthy. Additionally, Japan is focusing on drug discovery in China for economic growth.

MACRO AND CENTRAL BANKS: no major macro data releases today.

Let's pivot to the cryptocurrency markets. Bitcoin remains above sixty-four thousand dollars, with a 1.02% increase. Daily net inflows into Bitcoin ETFs were around $85.49 million. This movement could be influenced by recent statements about a possible peace agreement between Iran and Pakistan.

Regarding other cryptocurrencies, Ethereum is at $1675, with a 0.01% positive change. Solana gains 1.29%, reaching $68.2 BNB records a 1.07% increase, at $610.4

The Fear & Greed Index is at 18, in Extreme Fear territory, suggesting caution for investors.

No macro data on the agenda today. For a deeper dive into today's topics, find the full articles in the Top Stories section on our platform. Thanks for your attention, and we'll see you tomorrow.

articles.title: How Brexit has made Britain poorer – in charts
articles.snippet: Forecasters were wrong about an immediate recession but right that we would be worse off outside the EU As the 10th anniversary of the Brexit vote approaches, the verdict on Britain’s economic performance is clear: voting to leave has resulted in severe costs for households and businesses. The immediate recession predicted in the Treasury forecasts ordered by George Osborne – dubbed “ project fear ” by the Leave campaign – did not happen. The impact from the Covid pandemic, wars in Ukraine and Iran, and Donald Trump’s trade battles also cloud the picture. Continue reading...
